newsitem.title: USA: GM's Oldsmobile sees 10 pct 1997 sales gain.
newsitem.headline: GM's Oldsmobile sees 10 pct 1997 sales gain.

text.p: General Motors Corp's Oldsmobile Division said Wednesday that it expects U.S. sales to increase 10 percent in 1997 following a decline of 10.5 percent during 1996.
Oldsmobile General Manager Darwin Clark said the division's latest "centennial" products, including the all-new Cutlass sedan and Silhouette minivan will help revive the division's sales.
Oldsmobile sold 331,287 cars, minivans and sport/utility vehicles in 1996, down from 367,545 in 1995.
Clark said Oldsmobile planned to sell about 270,000 vehicles to retail buyers in 1997, with about 100,000 vehicles to corporate and rental fleets.
Oldsmobile, the U.S. auto industry's oldest surviving nameplate, celebrates its 100th anniversary in August, and has labeled its new products as centennial models.

Following the launch of the Cutlass and Silhouette, Oldsmobile introduces the all new Intrigue in the first and second quarter. The car replaces the Cutlass Suupreme, wheras the new Cutlass replaces the Ciera.
Cutlass brand manager Bob Clark (no relation to Darwin Clark) said he expects to sell about 40,000 to 45,000 of the new Cutlasses in 1997, and up to 75,000 next year.
Oldsmobile also Wednesday unveiled its Alero Alpha concept car, a precursor to the Alero coupe and sedan, which will replace the Achieva compact car line in about a year.
The Alero Alpha, a sleek, upscale coupe, takes styling cues from the Aurora luxury car and is aimed at buyers who are more well-to-do than current Achieva buyers. The
"This car will evolve into the production Alero, and they'll be reasonably close," said Oldsmobile spokesman August Buenz.

Bob Clark, also brand manager for the Achieva and Alero models, said the Alero will be aimed at buyers of upscale Japanese imports such as the Honda Accord and Acura Integra coupe. The coupe version of the Alero will be the only coupe that Oldsmobile offers in the future.
